::: {#sol-grad-norms}

::: {#fig-grad-norms}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Gradient norm against training step, on a log scale, for the pixel-by-pixel
#|   recurrent network. The norms mostly stay between 1 and 10 for the first
#|   500 or so steps, then spike to between 100 and over 1,000 several times,
#|   and settle near 1 for the last steps.
_ = plt.figure(figsize=(7, 3))
_ = plt.semilogy(rnn_norms, linewidth=0.7)
_ = plt.xlabel("training step")
_ = plt.ylabel("gradient norm")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
median_norm = np.median(rnn_norms)
max_norm_seen = max(rnn_norms)
share_above_10 = np.mean(np.array(rnn_norms) > 10)
```

The [norm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-inner-products.html#def-norm) of the [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) before each [training step](pytorch-basics.qmd#def-training-step) of the pixel reader.

:::

The median [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) [norm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-inner-products.html#def-norm) is `r sprintf("%.1f", py$median_norm)`,
but the largest is `r sprintf("%.0f", py$max_norm_seen)`,
`r sprintf("%.0f", py$max_norm_seen / py$median_norm)` times the median.
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$share_above_10)` of the steps have a norm above 10.

:::
